title: Customer Decision Brief — Integrated Rollout Options and Recommended Next Steps
body:
Executive summary:

This brief summarizes the technical findings and recommended rollout paths following the two-week integration POC with Customer X. The POC validated core accuracy and latency targets for the proposed assistant workflows, but revealed three material operational constraints: variable peak concurrency, intermittent sensitive-data routing requirements, and a sustained token-heavy evaluation workload that makes per-token hosted pricing expensive at scale.

Key outcomes from the POC:
- Model quality: prompt templates + light instruction tuning met the product accuracy bar (BLEU-like internal eval: 0.87 vs target 0.80) for primary user journeys.
- Latency: 95th percentile interactive latency averaged 320ms on the hosted testbed for short prompts; longer context sessions (12–16k tokens) experienced tail latency spikes up to 1.2s without KV cache warmup.
- Cost signal: simulated 1M monthly conversations would translate to ~ $35k–$55k/month on hosted tier given current token mix; dedicated reserved capacity estimate reduces unit cost by ~40% but requires 3–6 month commit.
- Security/ compliance: Customer X requires VPC egress controls for a subset of enterprise customers and a signed BAA for PHI data flows (legal in review).

Observed technical debt and operational gaps:
- Cache persistence: POC used ephemeral KV cache; would need warm-start and cross-request affinity for user sessions to avoid tail penalty.
- Autoscaling stability: burst tests showed cold-start impact during rapid concurrency ramps; warm pool sizing recommendations needed.
- Routing policies: current runtime can route by model variant, but config-level tooling for customer-specific routing rules is missing.

Deployment options evaluated (trade-offs):

1) Hosted-first, upgrade to Dedicated when volume stabilizes
- Description: Start on Redwood hosted API, instrument aggressively, then convert to Dedicated capacity when committed usage justifies it.
- Pros: Fast time-to-market, minimal ops overhead, no upfront infra commit; Redwood handles reliability and updates.
- Cons: Higher per-token costs at scale, limited network isolation for customers needing strict VPC controls (workarounds: IP allowlists + private links).
- Risk/mitigation: Cost creep — instrument token-level telemetry and set quota-based triggers for finance alert and auto-created Dedicated ROI evaluation.

2) Dedicated-reserved baseline + hosted burst
- Description: Commit to a Dedicated pool sized for 70% expected steady-state throughput; traffic bursts flow to hosted fallback.
- Pros: Predictable unit economics, stronger isolation, easier to meet latency SLOs during normal load. Hosted fallback keeps availability during unexpected peaks.
- Cons: Upfront contract and sizing risk; mis-sizing leads to wasted commit cost or sustained fallback.
- Risk/mitigation: Use initial 30-day usage runway and conservative autoscaling rules; include one canary week to validate sizing.

3) Private deployment (VPC + on-prem appliance) for regulated customers
- Description: Private control plane with customer-managed network, optional on-prem runtime for fully air-gapped environments.
- Pros: Meets strict compliance and VPC-only requirements; best for regulated pockets of Customer X’s customer base.
- Cons: Longest lead time (4–12 weeks), higher integration/maintenance effort, separate upgrade lifecycle.
- Risk/mitigation: Limit private to specific enterprise accounts; maintain a smaller managed Dedicated pool for the rest.

4) Hybrid edge-caching + central inference (recommended technical pattern)
- Description: Deploy lightweight edge cache/transform layer in customer region for prefix/KV caching + request shaping; central inference handled by Dedicated/Hosted.
- Pros: Reduces tail latency for long conversation contexts, preserves cost efficiency by centralizing heavy inference, eases VPC constraints when deployed inside customer VPC.
- Cons: Adds operational surface area and small infra footprint at edge site.

Recommendation (executive):
Given Customer X’s trajectory (fast user growth forecast, pockets of regulated customers, and an immediate need to ship product features within 4–6 weeks), we recommend a staged approach:
1) Launch on Hosted API with strict telemetry and guardrails — short-term (0–6 weeks). Validate user signal and token economics with production traffic.
2) Simultaneously prepare a Dedicated-reserved proposal targetting conversion at month 2–3 once commit thresholds hit (target: >500k paid conversation monthly or cost breakeven).
3) For regulated accounts, scope Private deployment as a scoped project (parallel, 6–12 week plan) and recommend edge caching inside customer VPC for data-in-transit control.

Concrete next steps (owners and timeline):
- Week 0–2 (Aisha / Solutions Eng): Deploy hosted production route with prod instrumentation, add token-level logging, enable quotas. Deliverable: telemetry dashboard + baseline cost report.
- Week 2–4 (Diego / Infra + Hannah / SRE): Implement warm pool sizing, KV cache persistence prototype (edge cache PoC), run two canary days of 2x expected concurrency. Deliverable: canary report with sizing recommendation.
- Week 4–6 (Ruth / Customer Success + Legal): Finalize BAA terms and VPC network design for regulated customers; draft private deployment SOW. Deliverable: SOW and legal sign-off checklist.
- Week 6–12 (Product + Sales): Prepare Dedicated-reserved contract proposal and migration runbook; schedule customer executive readout. Deliverable: Dedicated ROI model + migration playbook.

Success metrics to track (first 12 weeks):
- Cost: per-conversation unit cost and projected 3-month burn vs baseline target (target 30–40% reduction with Dedicated).
- Latency: 95p under 500ms for regular flows; under 800ms for long-context flows post-cache.
- Reliability: 99.9% availability for critical routes.
- Business: active enterprise trials onboarded (target 3) and signed SOW for one private deployment.

Estimated costs (order-of-magnitude):
- Hosted incremental run (observed in POC): $30k–$60k/month for 1M active conversations workload.
- Dedicated reserved (baseline sizing): $18k–$35k/month (commit-based, depends on GPU class and burst allowance).
- Private deployment: one-time integration/engineering ~ $60k–$120k + ongoing support/licensing ~ $15k–$40k/year.

Open decisions for exec review:
- Commit threshold: exact monthly committed spend that triggers Dedicated conversion (recommendation: 3-month rolling cost parity point).
- Private scope: how many regulated customers require on-prem vs VPC-only (affects build vs buy).
- SLA level and premium pricing for regulated customers (recommend A/B pricing tiers).

Appendix — workshop notes (selected bullets):
- Customer ops: asked for line-item telemetry that maps tokens to customer bill centers. Action: add billing tags in request metadata.
- Data handling: certain flows must redact PII before hitting shared logs — implemented in POC via pre-request hook prototype.
- Observability ask: per-route percentiles and token distribution charts; product agreed to add to Console dashboards.
- Integration gaps: OAuth connector to customer IAM has 2–3 missing scopes; Solutions Eng to PR a lighter-weight scope set.

Appendix — quick checklist for an initial hosted roll:
- Enable token-level tracing and dashboards (Aisha)
- Set hard quotas and billing alerts (Finance + Product Ops)
- Deploy KV cache warmup strategy (Infra)
- Schedule 2-day canary with 2x traffic (SRE)
- Legal: finalize BAA and minimal DPA addendum (Ruth)

Contact and escalation: Aisha Kapoor (lead) — aisha@redwood.ai, Diego Morales (infra) — diego@redwood.ai, Hannah Lee (SRE) — hannah@redwood.ai.

Notes and provenance: this document synthesizes findings from the POC lab logs (see linked artifacts), workshop cadence 2025-09-18 and 2025-09-24, and cost modeling done by finance. This is a working decision brief intended for the customer executive readout and internal GTM alignment.
